title: A cleared cache stays cleared

slide.title: clear() removes cache state, not pending results
slide.narrative:
- If the loader resolves after `clear()`, callers that hold the old promise still receive its value. `clear()` does not cancel the loader.
- The read retains its original generation. The new epoch blocks that completion from writing to `saved`.
- Cleanup checks promise identity. An old completion cannot remove a newer pending promise for the same key.

fileSummaries.summary: The current cache separates result delivery from storage through an epoch check and a promise identity check.

inlineExplanations.text: The epoch check controls storage, not result delivery. This return still supplies the loaded value to callers that hold the old promise.
After `clear()`, another read can store promise Q under the same key. Cleanup for old promise P leaves Q in place because their identities differ.

svgIllustration.title: State is cleared; the promise remains
svgIllustration.takeaway: The old promise delivers the value, but its generation cannot write to the cleared cache.
svgIllustration.assumptions: One cache miss starts a loader that later resolves. E names the captured epoch; P names the returned promise. No later read occurs in this sequence. Spacing does not show elapsed time. All participants are context. The caller implementation is not supplied.

entities.label: Caller
entities.summary: Holds the promise returned by read(); its implementation is not supplied.

entities.label: Revision cache
entities.summary: Owns saved, pending, priorities, bytes, and epoch.

entities.label: Async loader
entities.summary: Supplies the load promise. clear() does not cancel this operation.

relationships.label: read()
relationships.summary: Starts a read through the returned cache interface.

relationships.label: load()
relationships.summary: Calls the supplied loader after capturing the epoch.

relationships.label: return P
relationships.summary: Returns the promise chain independently of its entry in pending.

plan.question: Who receives the old result after clear(), and who controls cache storage?
plan.visualApproach: Use three fixed participants with downward time and a cache-owned state area below the cache lifeline. Keep the read history visible through clear() and completion.
plan.whyThisForm: Separate lifelines show that the caller retains P while clear() changes cache-owned state.
plan.encodings: Columns identify owners. Arrows show calls and result delivery. The outlined state area belongs to the cache. The captured generation appears separately because it belongs to the read closure.
plan.motion: Keep participants and earlier messages fixed. Show clear() while P and the load remain active. Then show loader resolution and the blocked storage operation before delivery through P.
plan.prediction: Another caller that already holds P also receives the resolved value. If a later read stores Q under the same pending key, cleanup for P leaves Q in place.
plan.restingState: The final frame retains the read, clear(), epoch mismatch, and result delivery.

scenarios.title: The loader resolves after clear()
scenarios.input: read() starts at epoch E; clear() runs before the loader resolves.

frames.caption: clear() advances epoch, empties the maps, and resets bytes. The caller still holds P, and the load remains active.
